Good evening, and welcome to the debate evening. A few rules before we start, and they are short. Each speaker has four minutes, not five, and I will stop you at four. After both speakers, the floor is open, and the only condition I insist on is that every objection be addressed to the argument and not to the person who made it. If you want to come in, raise a hand and wait. Do not talk over anybody, because the recording picks up nothing when two people speak at once and half the room hears nothing either. The motion tonight is that this country spends too little on public transport. Our first speaker proposes it, our second opposes it, and I would ask that the vote be taken at the end rather than now.

There is one move that changes how you are heard in English, and it costs you nothing. Before you disagree, concede something. One thing, and it has to be true. That is a fair point about the cost. You are right that nobody has explained the timing. Then you push back on the rest. What makes this work is not politeness, and I would say that most learners get this wrong. It works because it proves you were listening, and a room gives its attention to somebody who has just demonstrated that. The mistake to avoid is conceding something nobody claimed, which is a straw man and everybody can see it. And the second mistake is conceding everything, because then you have simply agreed and the conversation stops. One true, limited point. Then the word but, and then your argument.
